speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The recent attacks on Istanbul's Ataturk airport and in Nice underline that point.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The attack on a nightclub in Kuala Lumpur in June was the first Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS)-linked attack in Malaysia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Just over a week ago, Indonesian authorities arrested terror suspects in Batam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The main issue is not the nature of the plans – rockets and so on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The main point is that terrorists are looking for ways of attacking us – probing for entry points, checking out different options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These attacks can be launched by organised groups or self-radicalised individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They can plan and launch the attack from just outside Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They can come through our borders and checkpoints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Or they could be home-grown radicals launching an attack from within Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Even without firearms or explosives, they can still inflict many casualties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our security agencies are monitoring these developments closely, assessing the impact on Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We continue to work with our overseas partners to share information at all levels to fight against terrorism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The arrests in Batam by the Indonesians are just one example of this close cooperation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: When we receive information on such threats, we cannot always announce them publicly due to operational secrecy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our security agencies constantly calibrate our security measures in the context of such threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have previously spoken about the need to significantly enhance our national counter-terrorism efforts in areas of (a) increasing security protection and vigilance, (b) strengthening our security responses to an incident, and (c) building strong community resilience to fight terrorism under SG Secure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I will give an update on these measures as requested by the hon Member.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have commenced the roll-out of PolCam 2.0 and completed the installation of cameras in Ang Mo Kio Town Centre, Bedok Town Centre and Jurong Gateway.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In tandem, we have stepped up our efforts to encourage industry groups and premises owners to put in place security measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Safety and Security Watch Group (SSWG) is an important platform to achieve this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We held the first Counter-Terrorism seminar with the Retail SSWG in July, and with the Financial Industry SSWG last Friday, 12 August.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Through SSWG, the Singapore Police Force (SPF) advises premises owners on how to increase their vigilance through a customised approach for each industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Some practical examples of measures they can take include installing CCTVs or preparing their staff for emergencies through contingency plans, regular exercises and training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Owners of premises are encouraged to bring this training back to their workplaces and Police will follow up to help them review their plans and validate them through exercises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will hold more counter-terrorism seminars over the coming months for the hotel, chemical, security and manufacturing industries, amongst others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Police also work with various stakeholders to put in place security measures for crowded areas and events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I will not be able to go into the operational details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: But calibrated measures are taken to protect against attacks, including those which attempt to use a vehicle as a weapon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These measures are continually reviewed based on SPF's risk assessment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SPF has reorganised its terrorist response forces to enhance their firepower, operational capabilities and speed of response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SPF recently commissioned the first batch of Emergency Response Teams (ERTs) in June.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They are specially trained in counter-assault and equipped with more firepower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Singaporeans may have seen them patrolling in the Central Business District and Orchard areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SPF has also started operational trials for new Rapid Deployment Troops (RDT) within SPF's Special Operations Command in July.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The RDTs use Tactical Response Motorcycles to navigate through traffic to reach an incident quickly to support the ERTs in the event of an attack.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SPF and the Singapore Armed Forces are also jointly developing counter-terrorism plans for high-visibility patrols during heightened threat conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These provide both deterrence and swifter response to terrorist attacks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Third, the community plays a critical role in our efforts to fight terrorism on a sustained basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SG Secure will be officially launched later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SG Secure will sensitise, train and mobilise Singaporeans to play their part to prevent and deal with a terrorist attack.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Home Team has worked with our partner agencies to roll out pilot programmes across multiple domains to rally the community so that in the aftermath of a terrorist attack, we will stay united and strong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These programmes include the revamped Emergency Preparedness (EP) days held at Chong Pang, Jurong Spring and Toa Payoh West-Balestier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our security agencies will do all they can to prevent an attack.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: But should an attack occur, it is imperative for all of us to stand united against the threat, with a spirit of resilience that we will not be defeated and that we will bounce back as one people and one society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The first one is really about looking at the nature of various attacks that have been going on worldwide; the multi-centric or multi-site attacks seem to be the model of the day.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: So, how are we prepared in terms of having to respond to, perhaps, a multi-site attack and whether these have been put into consideration in our plans?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Therefore, our Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circle (IRCC) and our inter-faith and inter-race relations have been a model of our own and we have been working on it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It is a journey, really, and it does not stop.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How are we going to strengthen and perhaps have some further guidelines to deepen and strengthen this further to make sure that despite how many soft targets we have, the resilience of our inter-faith relations will remain the hard resilience to beat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Those are the kinds of attacks we have seen of late.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In that regard, the Member is quite right about the efforts by the IRCCs, by grassroots' networks, by community groups, by workplaces, by religious organisations to deepen that bond.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is not work that is happening today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is work that has been happening over the decades since our founding.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We need to make sure that we are prepared, not just to prevent an attack and to deal with it, but with the more fundamental questions about what the day after will be.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Will neighbours still trust one another, befriend one another or will there be an atmosphere of suspicion, of uncertainty?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is work that is painstaking and that requires stakeholders to look beyond the surface, look at the actual implementation to derive the objectives of a strong multi-cultural and multi-religious society.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also conduct exercises in specific areas, for example, in schools, to make sure that coordination is strong and robust and that measures are put in place.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some exercises are closed in that they relate principally to the Home Team and other coordinating forces but over the years, we have also been conducting public exercises of various scales.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We take the conducting of these exercises as well as the after-action review very seriously.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We make sure that we pin down all the learning points and ensure that the coordination within agencies and among agencies and with private stakeholders and the community, are strengthened.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: What is done last month or a year ago, we still need to do, going forward, with different groups of people, different work places, different community groups, neighbourhoods, schools and other institutions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, this is a major part of the SGSecure movement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I look forward to the Member's support and active participation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are two trends that I am quite concerned with today, especially when we see common place items being used, such as the knife attacks in Japan as well as in the recent Nice attack where a lorry was used to mow through the crowd.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How can we assure the public that with measures put in place operationally today, we are better prepared to protect our high-density areas, especially, from such attacks?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The second concern would be beyond our shores, like the Batam attack, that also showed us certain vulnerabilities today – that from beyond our shores, whether from the southern or northern neighbours, there is that vulnerability that exists.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What is the Ministry doing to better protect our nation?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member is right to articulate that attacks can come using everyday items, such as a vehicle, a knife, a brick, as much as they can involve fire power, guns, explosives, both makeshift and otherwise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is, as I said earlier, a challenge all of society needs to meet.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Strong intelligence, sharing, cooperation both within and with our partners around the world, are an important function of that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But so, too, are the support and vigilance of members of the community, making sure that Singaporeans without over-reacting and being overly suspicious, are alert enough to pick up threats early, pick up signs in the community that may point to people who might perhaps be led down the wrong path through what they see,  hear and read.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: What the Home Team has prepared for in terms of emergency response, I have articulated as best as I can without going into too much detail.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But prevention and response require the whole of society to play a part as could be seen from attacks in other countries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member also asked about threats beyond our shores.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are matters which the international communities are concerned about.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My Minister attended, very recently, a security dialogue and meeting with Malaysia, Indonesia and other countries in the Association for Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) the day after National Day.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is just an example of cooperation  with Malaysia and Indonesia, and with other jurisdictions as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier, it is not so much about the specific method that they are planning but rather the recognition that terrorists will try all ways and means and all forms to try to launch an attack on us.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We remain on the radar; we know that and we need to be prepared for that, both at the level of the security forces but also making sure the community is entirely on board with us.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: He had shared about the number of PolCams to be installed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Would the Senior Minister of State be able to share what percentage of the island would be covered by security cameras or sensors for surveillance use, given possible collaboration of the Smart Nation Office?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These have been implemented with a lot of care to ensure that the privacy concerns of residents are addressed in a way that they have welcomed this measure because of the security and sense of assuredness that are provided to them, the balance has been struck right.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Those cameras have helped to solve a number of cases in the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, crime has been reduced by a certain amount.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As a result of these cameras, there has been a deterrent effect and, in post-incident investigations, they have been helpful.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member asked what percentage of the island will be covered by PolCam 2.0.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I cannot give you a land area percentage but I have just articulated the places which will be covered: places with a high flow of people, the cameras will help us in addressing and preventing crime, and also play a very important role in counter-terrorism.
